description: A coordination framework among the Union and other middle powers holding pieces of the AI supply chain — export-licence alignment, joint bargaining over compute access, shared evaluation capacity. Nobody cedes sovereignty to it, but together its members can withhold things even the great powers need. It counts as securing access on the terms of metric rule 5, and moves `eu_political_capital` on the terms of metric rule 6.

Protests against AI energy use escalate into coordinated civil disobedience targeting data centres in multiple member states, with sustained blockades and acts of sabotage. The movement frames AI as an existential climate threat, and local governments face pressure to halt expansions. This further strains public sentiment and complicates infrastructure planning.

A coordinated effort among Germany, Poland, and the Netherlands forms to establish a shared open-weight model repository and evaluation hub using existing academic and national lab infrastructure, aiming to counter dependency on US-controlled models. Driven by recent sovereignty failures and rising political capital pressure, the initiative gains traction as a pragmatic workaround.

Public protests against AI energy consumption escalate into coordinated civil disobedience targeting data centre construction sites in three member states, with arrests and political condemnation. The movement frames AI as ecologically extractive, drawing support from green parties and youth movements.

A coordinated movement of regional governments, civil society groups, and mid-tier tech firms within the EU forms to resist centralised AI infrastructure projects they see as environmentally unsustainable and politically illegitimate. Sparked by the failed Saclay and Wrocław projects and amplified by the emergent_ai_power_protests, the coalition blocks new data centre developments in multiple member states, delays EU compute procurement, and demands democratic oversight of AI sovereignty initiatives. This is not a single event but a spreading institutional resistance.

Amid rising energy concerns and stalled sovereignty projects, a consortium of European energy regulators and grid operators issues an emergency joint report warning that unchecked AI compute growth threatens grid stability and climate targets. The report triggers immediate national scrutiny of data centre power contracts and calls for binding EU-wide efficiency standards, reframing AI policy around energy security rather than just competitiveness or safety.
